epigraph.quote: A falling knife has no handle, but a stock pulling back to a rising institutional shelf eventually builds a floor—if you wait for the floor to hold before stepping onto it.
epigraph.author: Weinstein Stage Analysis Maxim

web_blocks.html: Even a sound post-demerger restructuring thesis fails if you buy into post-earnings distribution without tape confirmation. On the November 13, 2026 ledger cutoff, INDIAGLYCO closed at ₹311.30 [23]. In the separate post-cutoff November 16, 2026 session, TradingView quoted the stock at ₹292.45 (-6.06%), extending its 1-month slide to -10.97% as shares digested Q2 FY27 continuing-operations results [2][4][23].

Reconciling the Weinstein stage requires separating unadjusted vs. demerger-adjusted price histories [23]. Our facts_IN_2026-11-13.json feed (Yahoo unadjusted pre-demerger price history) shows a 50-DMA of ₹319.33, 200-DMA of ₹827.22, and 52W High of ₹1,222.00, classifying INDIAGLYCO as Stage 4 (Markdown) (RSI14 42.38) [23]. By contrast, TradingView's demerger-adjusted series adjusts prior history for the spin-off, showing a 50-DMA of ₹304.54, 200-DMA of ₹231.15, 30W SMA of ₹253.05, and 52W High of ₹399.00 (52W Low ₹163.68) [23]. On that adjusted series, our deterministic engine classifies INDIAGLYCO in STAGE_3 consolidation with a hard gate of CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT—and zero basis to treat it as Stage 2 [23]. At the November 13 close of ₹311.30, price sat -2.51% below Yahoo's unadjusted 50-DMA and +2.22% above TradingView's adjusted 50-DMA, before slipping to ₹292.45 on November 16 [23].

web_blocks.title: Tape Discipline: Why Buying ₹311.30 (or Post-Cutoff ₹292.45) Fails the Multi-Timeframe Test
paragraphs: Short- and medium-term momentum gauges warn against premature entry [23]. At the November 13 close of ₹311.30, price sat below Yahoo's unadjusted 50-DMA (₹319.33, Stage 4). On the post-cutoff November 16 TradingView quote (₹292.45, -6.06%), it also broke below the adjusted 50-DMA (₹304.54), 10-week EMA (₹300.04), and 4H EMA20 (₹307.75) with 4H RSI at 38.56.

To earn an entry, we need two sequential confirmations [23]. First, price must test into the ₹269.72–₹277.94 support zone around Pivot S1 (₹273.83). Second, the 4H chart must print a higher low or reclaim the 4H EMA20 on expanding volume. Until then, cash stays on the sidelines.

web_blocks.html: Volume behavior also reinforces patience [23]. Recent daily volume of 454,130 shares sits at just 0.25x the 30-day average of 1,809,940 shares (and slightly below the 10-day average of 480,515 shares). The post-demerger institutional repositioning spike has faded into a lower-liquidity air pocket [23]. With a 14-day ATR of ₹19.61 (~6.3% of ₹311.30) and Bollinger Band width at 19.86%, intraday swings remain wide enough to punish premature entries above ₹280. Waiting for a test of the ₹269.72–₹277.94 zone lets volatility work in our favor rather than against our stop [23].

book_paragraphs: Valuation tells us what a business is worth; the tape tells us when other market participants are finished selling it. For India Glycols Limited, the chart as of the November 13, 2026 ledger close of ₹311.30—and the subsequent post-cutoff November 16 TradingView quote of ₹292.45, down 6.06%—delivers a clear message: stand aside for now and let the post-demerger digestion finish.

When you and I reconcile the multi-timeframe picture, we first have to resolve a data-feed quirk that trips up many investors after a demerger. Our facts_IN_2026-11-13.json feed uses Yahoo's unadjusted pre-demerger price history, which shows a 50-day moving average of ₹319.33, a 200-day moving average of ₹827.22, and a 52-week high of ₹1,222.00—classifying INDIAGLYCO as Stage 4 (Markdown) with RSI14 at 42.38. By contrast, TradingView's demerger-adjusted series adjusts historical prices for the spin-off, showing a 50-DMA of ₹304.54, a 200-DMA of ₹231.15, a 30-week SMA of ₹253.05, and a 52-week high of ₹399.00.

On TradingView's demerger-adjusted series, our deterministic engine classifies INDIAGLYCO in Weinstein Stage 3 consolidation, triggering our hard technical gate: CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. At the November 13 close of ₹311.30, the stock sat 2.51% below Yahoo's unadjusted 50-DMA and 2.22% above TradingView's adjusted 50-DMA. By the post-cutoff November 16 quote of ₹292.45, it had broken below both TradingView's 50-DMA (₹304.54) and 10-week EMA (₹300.04), with 4H RSI sitting at a weak 38.56. Either way you slice it, the stock is not in Stage 2 and has no confirmed intraday turn.

Our options and liquidity audit also confirms a practical constraint: INDIAGLYCO is not part of the NSE Futures and Options segment. There is no liquid listed options chain, which means you cannot sell cash-secured puts at support or structure defined-risk call spreads to play a bounce. Every rupee of exposure must be taken in cash equity, where your only protection against a deeper drawdown is entry price discipline and a hard stop-loss.

Fortunately, the chart gives us a very clean structural shelf just below current levels. Pivot S1 sits at ₹273.83, anchoring a defined support buy zone between ₹269.72 and ₹277.94. Notice how well that zone aligns with the broader volatility profile: with a 14-day Average True Range of ₹19.61, a normal 1-ATR pullback from the post-cutoff ₹292.45 level lands directly inside that ₹269.72–₹277.94 band. Below that shelf, our structural invalidation stop sits at ₹243.25—comfortably underneath the rising 30-week moving average at ₹253.05. If the stock slices through ₹243.25 on a closing basis, the Stage 3 consolidation has failed into a Stage 4 downtrend, and we want no part of it.

Notice also what is happening beneath the surface in the shareholding and market regime data. Per Screener's September 2026 disclosures, promoters hold a steady 59.63% with Nil pledged shares, while public shareholder count has consolidated from 1,41,417 in December 2023 down to 60,112 by September 2026—a sign that weaker retail hands have rotated out, while FIIs hold 2.77% and DIIs hold 3.06%. Meanwhile, the Nifty 50 sits in an Uptrend with narrow breadth (79.2% of the breadth pool above their 50-day averages, with 3 distribution days in the last 25 sessions). In a narrow-breadth market, stocks that miss near-term earnings expectations often overshoot to support before finding institutional bids.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Volume Cooling and Volatility Envelope
paragraphs: One of the most telling clues on INDIAGLYCO's chart is what happened to trading volume after the September 2026 demerger dust settled. Over the past 30 trading days, average daily volume ran at roughly 1.81 million shares as arbitrageurs, index funds, and special-situations desks adjusted their books for the record date and ex-demerger listing. By mid-November 2026, however, daily volume had cooled to 454,130 shares—just 0.25x of that 30-day average and slightly below the 10-day average of 480,515 shares.

When volume dries up to a quarter of its recent event average while price slips 6.06% on the post-cutoff November 16 session to ₹292.45, it tells you two things. First, aggressive institutional accumulation is not stepping in above ₹290; buyers are content to let sellers come down to them. Second, because the 14-day Average True Range sits at ₹19.61—roughly 6.3% of the ₹311.30 ledger close—and Bollinger Band width is wide at 19.86%, the stock can easily travel ₹15 to ₹25 in a couple of sessions without any major news.

That is why placing a buy order at ₹311.30—or even chasing the post-cutoff ₹292.45 print—is poor craft. On the post-cutoff tape, ₹292.45 sits ₹12.09 below TradingView's 50-day moving average (₹304.54), which now acts as overhead resistance, and ₹18.62 above Pivot S1 (₹273.83), which is the nearest genuine demand shelf. In a narrow-breadth Nifty 50 uptrend, capital rotates ruthlessly out of stocks that lose their 50-DMA until they find real support.

book_subsections.title: The Exact Two-Step Confirmation Protocol at ₹269.72–₹277.94
paragraphs: So what does a textbook, high-probability entry actually look like from here? We define our support buy zone between ₹269.72 and ₹277.94, straddling Pivot S1 at ₹273.83 and sitting comfortably above the rising 30-week moving average at ₹253.05. Remember that our invalidation stop is anchored at ₹243.25—below the 30-week SMA—because if INDIAGLYCO loses its 30-week trendline on a weekly closing basis, the entire Stage 3 consolidation has morphed into a Stage 4 breakdown.

To avoid catching a falling knife inside that ₹269.72–₹277.94 zone, we require two sequential confirmations on the four-hour chart. First, price must actually reach or test into the ₹269.72–₹277.94 band, burning off the remaining short-term selling pressure. Second, the four-hour chart must print a higher low or reclaim its 4H 20-EMA (currently ₹307.75, which will drift lower as price consolidates) accompanied by a turn up in 4H RSI from sub-40 levels and expanding volume. Without that 4H turn, even a cheap support level can turn into a trapdoor—especially in a cash-equity-only stock with no NSE F&O hedging tools.

book_subsections.title: Mapping the Full Moving-Average and Pivot Ladder
paragraphs: To trade this setup without emotion, it helps to visualize the entire price ladder on TradingView's demerger-adjusted series from the 52-week high down to the primary long-term floor. At the top sits the adjusted 52-week high of ₹399.00 and Pivot R1 at ₹394.28, with Pivot R2 overhead at ₹456.87 (while Yahoo's unadjusted pre-demerger series shows a 52-week high of ₹1,222.00 and 200-DMA of ₹827.22). Below Pivot Middle at ₹336.42 sits a dense cluster of short- and medium-term moving averages: Yahoo's unadjusted 50-DMA at ₹319.33, the 4H 50-SMA at ₹315.61, the 20-day SMA at ₹311.39, the 10-day SMA at ₹308.44, the 4H 20-EMA at ₹307.75, TradingView's 50-day SMA at ₹304.54, and the 10-week EMA at ₹300.04.

Notice how that overhead supply band behaves: at the November 13 close of ₹311.30, INDIAGLYCO was already capped below Yahoo's unadjusted 50-DMA (₹319.33) and the 4H 50-SMA (₹315.61). On the post-cutoff November 16 quote of ₹292.45, it slipped underneath TradingView's 50-DMA (₹304.54) and 10-week EMA (₹300.04) as well. That entire ₹300 to ₹319 band now acts as overhead supply until reclaimed on strong volume.

Below ₹292.45, however, the structural picture is far more constructive. Pivot S1 stands at ₹273.83, forming the center of our ₹269.72–₹277.94 support buy zone. Roughly ₹20 below that sits the rising 30-week SMA at ₹253.05, followed by our invalidation stop at ₹243.25, TradingView's 200-day SMA at ₹231.15, Pivot S2 at ₹215.97, and the adjusted 52-week low at ₹163.68. By waiting for price to drop into ₹269.72–₹277.94, you are positioning yourself right above three major institutional trendlines—Pivot S1, the 30-week SMA, and the 200-day SMA—while letting the overhead sellers exhaust themselves first.

This reconciliation also explains why you should never blindly rely on a single unadjusted screener label after a demerger. Yahoo's unadjusted series marks INDIAGLYCO as Stage 4 because it compares ₹311.30 against pre-demerger prices near ₹1,222.00, whereas TradingView's demerger-adjusted series classifies it as Stage 3 consolidation (CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT). Neither feed shows a Stage 2 uptrend—and both lead to the exact same conclusion: keep your powder dry until support holds.

book_subsections.title: Shareholding Rotation and Why Patience Beats Chasing Post-Demerger Volatility
paragraphs: Examining Screener's September 2026 shareholding pattern adds helpful context to the technical tape. Promoter holding stands at a rock-solid 59.63% with Nil pledged shares reported in the BSE XBRL filing. At the same time, the total number of public shareholders has consolidated from 1,41,417 in December 2023 down to 60,112 in September 2026. Meanwhile, FIIs hold 2.77% and DIIs hold 3.06%.

What does that tell you and I about market microstructure? It tells us that INDIAGLYCO is still a relatively under-owned mid-cap chemical stock where large domestic mutual funds have not yet built major institutional positions, and where post-demerger price discovery is driven largely by HNIs, family offices, and active momentum desks. In stocks with 5.83% combined FII and DII ownership, post-earnings air pockets like the -6.06% drop on November 16 can extend further than expected before stabilizing, simply because there is no passive institutional bid sitting under every 2% dip.

Yet that exact lack of crowded institutional ownership also creates opportunity once the chart settles. When a stock with a 59.63% unpledged promoter base pulls back into a clear technical shelf like Pivot S1 at ₹273.83 on 0.25x average volume, selling pressure tends to exhaust itself quickly. By waiting for the ₹269.72–₹277.94 zone and requiring a 4-hour reversal confirmation, you avoid becoming exit liquidity for post-earnings sellers and instead step in right alongside early accumulation.

book_subsections.title: Why Cash-Equity-Only Execution Raises the Bar for Entry Timing
paragraphs: In liquid F&O names, an options desk can sometimes absorb imprecise entry timing by selling out-of-the-money cash-secured puts at support or structuring a defined-risk bull call spread. Because INDIAGLYCO has no listed derivatives contract on the NSE, those tools are completely off the table. Every single share you buy carries full one-for-one equity delta from the moment your order fills.

Compare INDIAGLYCO's current tape with IG Petrochemicals (IGPL) in the same chemical peer group. IGPL sits in a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend at ₹554.80, trading +0.81% above its 10-week EMA (₹550.35) with Weekly RSI at 57.02. INDIAGLYCO, by contrast, is sitting -2.53% below its 10-week EMA (₹300.04) and -3.97% below its 50-day SMA (₹304.54), with 4-hour RSI at 38.56. That contrast explains why IGPL passes the immediate Stage 2 timing screen while INDIAGLYCO is gated at CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. Respecting that gate—waiting for ₹269.72–₹277.94 and a confirmed 4-hour turn—is how you manufacture options-like asymmetry in a cash-equity-only stock.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Let the 4-Hour Chart Confirm the Floor
book_callouts.text: Watching a stock drop 6% in a day toward a well-defined support shelf at ₹273.83 can tempt you into placing blind limit orders and walking away. Resist that urge. Because INDIAGLYCO has no F&O hedge and its 4H RSI is still sliding at 38.56, we want to see price enter the ₹269.72–₹277.94 zone, stabilize, and print a higher low or reclaim its 4H 20-EMA on expanding volume before committing capital.
